## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
GE Vernova/APM was on site to perform a HGPI & 7FA.04 AGP full tech upgrade on 7FA.04 
Gas Turbine SN 297651 and T&I on 7FH2 Hydrogen Cooled Generator SN 337X766 at OPC 
T.A Smith Station on March 26, 2024. Scope of the work was conducted on 1 x 12 hours 
shifts, 7 days a week with 1 day off every 14th day of outage. GE Vernova/ APM supplied 
tooling, technical direction, and craft labor. The HGP Inspection work scope was including 
FMI F6775G20 AGP Full Tech Package HGP Capitals, 32K capable hot gas path components, 
7FA AGP 1AO 2FO 2AO Thermocouples, TTKX Coefficient Modification, Updated exhaust 
temperature control curve, S1N Inner Support Ring, and Water Wash Skid and Gen II retrofit.
LOTO and work permit was received for roof works on March 30th at 1:00 pm and began 
disassembly. 
The following Engineering Request (ER) cases were opened/referenced during this outage: 
·       ER-20240402-1102 Compressor Borescope Inspection Report
·       ER-20240413-0171 AFS Aft Fuel Staging hardware evaluation.
·       ER-20240419-1320 297651 - AFS Fuel Post Nut Galling/Destructive Nut Removal
·       ER-20240416-1950 TP AFS bracket mounting holes drilled in wrong position - 
·       ER-20240417-1903 Product Services CMU Clearance Evaluation
TIL's incorporated, referenced and/or verified during this outage include:
·       TIL 2484: 7F DLN 2.6+ COMBUSTION CAN WASHER DISTRESS. Changeout of washer 
material for forward to aft casings and aft to CDC flanges. Part Number: 310T0901P0002 
and 310T0901P0001
·       TIL 2049-R2: IGVs observed with rub on the rub ring near the RHJ.
·       TIL 2363-R1: IGVs observed with multiple bushing migrations. Site re-staked the 
bushings during this outage.
·       TIL 1509-R4: R0 observed with casing rubs on the lower half, upper half, RHJ, and 
LHJ. R0 tip NDI performed. No defect reported during this outage.
·       TIL 1870-R2: First row compressor blades observed with no staking defects.
·       TIL 1562-R1: Shims observed with no defects.

## EHS SUMMARY
In the commitment by GE Vernova to SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) safety comes 
first: making sure all our employees and contributors go home safely from work is our 
imperative. Our culture values safety and requires everyone’s commitment to preventing any 
harm, injury, or loss of life. For that purpose, GE Vernova has safety standards (Life Saving 
Rules) and policies in place.
An EHS plan was implemented and carried out during this outage. EHS specialists were 
onsite and conducted safety meetings before each shift began. Job safety analysis forms 
were also filled out before the start of each task. All personnel working on equipment 
followed the proper LOTO procedures before work began as well as after work completed. 
Lift plans were created and approved before any critical lifts were performed. During the 
outage, no safety violations or near misses were recorded.
GE Vernova critical lifting plans were reviewed & approved by plant’s 3rd party vendor 
[ MESA] to assure safe lifting during the outage.

Part Description:

Electrical Testing and a Borescope Inspection were conducted on the unit.     Results are

attached for reference.     This unit is fit to be returned to service.

The following electrical tests were conducted on the generator stator and field, all with

results which are well within the GE passing criteria.

•  Stator IR and PI Megger Tests - 1 min PI values were 3.19GOhm, 3.16GOhm and

3.14GOhm respectively (GE criteria is 1GOhm)     PI values came in at 7.04, 6.8 and 6.76

(GE criteria is 2).

•  Stator DC Leakage Tests / Hi-Pot Tests gave leakage currents of  3.5microA,

3.0microA and 3.5microA respectively @ 40KVDC.    Values under 100microA are

considered good.

•  Stator Armature Winding Resistance values were 0.001220Ohm, 0.001217Ohm and

0.001216Ohm @ 16C which when converted to 25C is very close to the factory 0.001290

value @ 25C.

•  Field Tests came out well with a straight line AC Impedance curve, 2.04 GOhm IR and

3.8 PI plus a winding resistance of 0.1374 Ohm with factory value being 0.1412 @ 25C.

•     A Borescope Inspection was also conducted which showed the stator TE and CE

End-Windings to be in good shape.     Furthermore, all hardware was found to be secure

and in place.    See attached report for more details.

GE Gas Power

Foreword

This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the generator described in the Site and Unit

Information section with respect to normal wear, greasing, dusting, oil contamination, corona, hot spots, arcing,

rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other

abnormal conditions.

Color images depicting the condition of the generator were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor

Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the generator was illuminated

using an external light source.

The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed

for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the

magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also

important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by

lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a

photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual

condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section

of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs

should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography.

Foreword

This report describes and documents the borescope inspection of the turbine described in the Site and Unit

Information section with respect to normal wear, rubs, fouling, depositing, oxidation, erosion, spallation,

cracking, missing material, foreign object damage and other abnormal conditions.

Color images depicting the condition of the turbine were captured using the Waygate technologies’ Mentor

Visual iQ Videoscope System with a 4.5m X 6.1mm flexible probe.  The interior of the turbine was illuminated

using an external light source.

The images included in the photo report show typical, and/or abnormal, conditions of the components observed

for documentation and comparison during future inspections.  It is important to note that due to the

magnification of the lens, object viewed through the videoscope may be significantly magnified.  It is also

important to note that videoscopes have certain minor imperfections inherent in their construction, caused by

lens distortion.  As a result, a surface, which is straight or true, may seem to appear slightly curved in a

photograph.  This is no problem for the inspector since multiple views and close-ups easily yield the actual

condition of the area.  However, due to the possibility of optical distortion, judgments concerning any section

of component of the turbine are best made at the time of the examination.  Interpretation of the photographs

should be made by someone familiar with videoscope photography.

Unit Access

Access to the compressor was gained by entering through the inlet plenum where the inlet guide vanes and

the first fifteen rotating and stationary stages were inspected.  Access to stages 15, 16, 17, and EGV1 was

gained though the opened right side CDC ports.

TIL 2049-R2 : IGVs observed with rub on the rub ring near the RHJ.

TIL 2363-R1 : IGVs observed with multiple bushing migrations.  Site is planning to re-stake the bushings during

this outage.

TIL 1509-R4 : R0 observed with casing rubs on the lower half, upper half, RHJ, and LHJ.  No other defects

noted.

TIL 1870-R2 : First row compressor blades observed with no staking defects.

TIL 1562-R1 : Shims observed with no defects.

ETC 294 : S2 vanes observed with no defects.

TIL 2286 : S5 vanes observed with no defects.

TIL 1769 : Aft stators observed with base misalignment measuring .023”.

TIL 1502-2R1 : Aft compressor observed with casing rubs.  See the comments below for reference.

TIL 1850-R3 : Shrouded S17 vanes observed with no defects other than the previously mention base

misalignment.

Note : Deposits observed on the S0 vanes through the S8 vanes.  Corrosion observed on the R9 blades through

the EGVs.

R2 blades observed with (x1) LE PS FOD.

Lower case rub observed on the R5, R6, R8, R12, R13, R14, and R15 blades.

S7 vanes observed with base rocking measuring .046”.

S8 vanes observed with tip rotor rub and base rocking measuring .038”.

R9 blades observed with multiple LE SS/PS FOD.

S14 and S15 vanes observed with base twisting.

R15 blades also observed with RHJ casing rub.

R16 blades observed with multiple LE PS FOD.

### 3.4.1 Combustion Liners
F
O
R
M
Inspection Type: Visual
Part Condition: Fair
Part Description: 
Combustion liners were removed and visually inspected for weld cracks, spring seal 
condition, distortion, stop wear and collar wear as part of the outage scope. Typical TBC 
discoloration was observed on liner bodies from exposures to heat with typical wear on the 
stops and crossfire tube collars. The spring seals were inspected and found to be in good 
condition. Typical minor wear was observed on the spring seals at the engagement point 
with transition piece. All flame detector collars, and each spark plugs floating collars 
functioned properly. No other indications were observed at the time of inspection. The liners 
were replaced with a refurbished set of components at assembly. The service-run set of 
liners was sent to a GE service center for further inspection, repair, and refurbishment.
Recommendation Status: Should be planned for next Outage
Recommendation Type: Repairs
Recommendation Description: 
Visually inspect and report condition on next outage. New / refurbished set should be onsite 
to replace the liner set if reached the max recommended operation hours. monitor the TBC 
condition during the annual borescope inspection and report any finding to GE Vernona 
representative for further support.      
GEGEGE

replacement and plan to be inspected next operational cycle. TPs setback clearances were 
checked for reassembly. All values were reviewed and found to be within the acceptable 
limits. Refer to the attached inspection sheets below.

correct numbers, based on site records.

APPLICATION

PURPOSE 
This TIL is to inform users to update the DC fault Trip amps settings in the exciter software in 
order to reduce the arc flash potential energy with the intent to reduce damage caused to the 
collector components during a collector flashover event and also to estimate the appropriate PPE 
requirements for online collector maintenance.

## BACKGROUND DISCUSSION
The purpose of the collector is to transmit the excitation current from the exciter to the 
generator field with the help of carbon brushes riding on a collector ring. The collector system 
consists of the collector (slip) rings, brushes, and collector connections with the field winding. 
Carbon brushes pass the DC excitation current onto the collector rings by contact via thin 
conducting film that is formed under normal operating conditions. Maintaining the collector in 
proper condition largely entails preserving the current-carrying film. Collector Flashover events 
can lead to significant damage to the slip ring, brush rigging assemblies, and the metal shaft. The 
term collector flashover describes an unwanted opening of the highly inductive generator field 
circuit at either one or both collector poles. Breakdown of the insulation separating the two 
polarities that are at different electrical potential is a very rare occurrence. Typically, arcing is 
caused by a progressive loss of contact between the ring and brushes,

causing current to arc across the gap until the gap becomes too large for the arc to be sustained. 
This action is like slowly opening a knife switch in an inductive circuit. The arcing can go on for 
hours, even days, before the field circuit opens, ending the flashover event. 
Flashover events have been part of the power industry since the first use of slip rings (collector 
rings). Most flashover events may be avoided with proper preventative maintenance as 
described in the operations and maintenance manuals. 
In the static exciter (EX2100*/EX2100e*) software, the parameter DC_FaultOC (DC Fault trip 
amps) is the DC current level (amps) that will cause instantaneous over-current to become active 
and trip the exciter. This value is typically kept at less than five times the shunt rating. This value 
(<5 x ShuntAmps) was originally configured by considering the equipment's withstanding. 
capability during such over-current events. The hazard of exposure to the arc flash energy can be 
limited by reducing the field over-current trip settings, which reduces and limits the maximum 
field current that flows during an arcing event and thus reduces the arc flash energy. 
RECOMMENDATIONS 
In order to reduce the arc flash energy during some collector flashover event conditions, it is 
recommended for units subject to this TIL to reduce the DC Fault trip amps to three times the 
shunt rating in the exciter software followed by download of software to all controllers (M1, M2, 
and C) and reboot.

times the ShuntAms value. To comply with this TIL, it is recommended to modify DC_FaultOC for

2-The ShuntAmps is 2500Adc and the DC fault trip amps (DC_FaultOC) is 11250Adc, which is 4.5 
times the ShuntAms value. To comply with this TIL, it is recommended to modify DC_FaultOC for  
modify DC_FaultOC for (X1 &X2) from 11250Adc to 7500Adc.   
Lastly, after completing the above recommendations it is also advised to recalculate the arc-flash 
potential requirements to ensure that the maintenance personnel have the right level of PPE 
required to perform online maintenance of the collector. GEK116362 section II Safety can be 
referred for further details. 
This TIL is considered complete when the parameter DC_FaultOC is updated, and software is 
downloaded to the controllers followed by a reboot.
